items.title: H = {x = 0} is noncharacteristic for Q
items.label: prop:noncar
items.correspondence: The pinned formal source defines noncharacteristic finiteness by the cokernel module and proves its equivalence to finiteness of the literal restricted coordinate ring R/(J+(x₀)). It proves that finiteness for the canonical annihilator and separately proves the zero-section support conclusion in prime-spectrum form. For the paper's intermediate finite-projection claim, `canonicalPrincipalHypersurfaceIdeal` is defined as the sum of the principal ideal generated by `presentedPrincipalComponent k orderWeight N d` (the canonical principal symbol P after the monic chart) and the ideal generated by Lean's normal coordinate `X (.inl 0)` (paper x₁). `canonical_principal_hypersurface_finite` states that the resulting full-symbol-ring quotient is finite as a module over `oldTangentialCoeffRing` T. The `normalMomentumPolynomialEquiv_tangentialMap` bridge identifies the induced T-action with the canonical tangential-coordinate inclusion. Thus the formal result covers the literal algebraic finite-map clause, though it does not state the paper's particular generating list 1, ξ₁, …, ξ₁^{N−1}.
